claim: STAT5 is encoded by two genes, Stat5a and Stat5b, derived from a relatively recent duplication event.
source: In mammals, STAT5 is unique because it is encoded by two genes, termed Stat5a and Stat5b, derived from a relatively recent duplication event (Wang and Levy, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang and Levy, 2012.

claim: The ancestral STAT5 gene duplicated on two separate occasions during vertebrate evolution.
source: In fact, the ancestral STAT5 gene appears to have duplicated on two separate occasions during vertebrate evolution. Once in teleosts, resulting in two paralogs on different chromosomes, and again in eutherians, resulting in the two contiguous mammalian paralogs (Liongue et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Liongue et al., 2012.

claim: STAT5A and STAT5B are homologous at the DNA, RNA and protein levels.
source: Because of their recent divergence, STAT5A and STAT5B are homologous at the DNA, RNA and protein levels, which has led to persisting questions about whether they are redundant or functionally distinct.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the recent divergence of the paralogs.

claim: Stat5a-deficient mice exhibit poor mammary function.
source: Stat5a-deficient mice exhibit poor mammary function (Liu et al., 1997), reduced hematopoietic stem cell proliferation (Zhang et al., 2000) and diminished antibody class switching (Kagami et al., 2000)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 1997.

claim: Stat5a-deficient mice exhibit reduced hematopoietic stem cell proliferation.
source: Stat5a-deficient mice exhibit poor mammary function (Liu et al., 1997), reduced hematopoietic stem cell proliferation (Zhang et al., 2000) and diminished antibody class switching (Kagami et al., 2000)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2000.

claim: Stat5a-deficient mice exhibit diminished antibody class switching.
source: Stat5a-deficient mice exhibit poor mammary function (Liu et al., 1997), reduced hematopoietic stem cell proliferation (Zhang et al., 2000) and diminished antibody class switching (Kagami et al., 2000)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kagami et al., 2000.

claim: Stat5b-deficient mice exhibit dwarfism.
source: while Stat5b-deficient mice exhibit dwarfism (Udy et al., 1997), more pronounced lymphopenia, and greater defects in cytokine-driven lymphocyte proliferation (Moriggl et al., 1999b; Imada et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Udy et al., 1997.

claim: Stat5b-deficient mice exhibit more pronounced lymphopenia than Stat5a-deficient mice.
source: while Stat5b-deficient mice exhibit dwarfism (Udy et al., 1997), more pronounced lymphopenia, and greater defects in cytokine-driven lymphocyte proliferation (Moriggl et al., 1999b; Imada et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Moriggl et al., 1999b and Imada et al., 1998.

claim: Stat5b-deficient mice exhibit greater defects in cytokine-driven lymphocyte proliferation than Stat5a-deficient mice.
source: while Stat5b-deficient mice exhibit dwarfism (Udy et al., 1997), more pronounced lymphopenia, and greater defects in cytokine-driven lymphocyte proliferation (Moriggl et al., 1999b; Imada et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Moriggl et al., 1999b and Imada et al., 1998.

claim: Deletion of Stat5a and Stat5b has comparable effects on eosinophil recruitment.
source: On the other hand, deletion of Stat5a and Stat5b has comparable effects on some physiological processes, such as eosinophil recruitment (Kagami et al., 2000)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kagami et al., 2000.

claim: Infertility, anemia and perinatal lethality are evident only in mice lacking both Stat5a and Stat5b paralogs.
source: and the most dramatic phenotypes, such as infertility, anemia and perinatal lethality, are evident only in mice lacking both paralogs, which implies redundancy and/or cooperativity (Teglund et al., 1998; Socolovsky et al., 1999; Cui et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Teglund et al., 1998; Socolovsky et al., 1999; Cui et al., 2004.

claim: The target repertoires for STAT5A and STAT5B mostly overlap.
source: The target repertoires for STAT5A and STAT5B mostly overlap, which implies redundancy, but there are also a subset of sites that may be differentially bound, which implies specificity (Liao et al., 2008; 2011; Yamaji et al., 2013; Kanai et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liao et al., 2008; 2011; Yamaji et al., 2013; Kanai et al., 2014.

claim: There are a subset of sites that may be differentially bound by STAT5A and STAT5B.
source: The target repertoires for STAT5A and STAT5B mostly overlap, which implies redundancy, but there are also a subset of sites that may be differentially bound, which implies specificity (Liao et al., 2008; 2011; Yamaji et al., 2013; Kanai et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liao et al., 2008; 2011; Yamaji et al., 2013; Kanai et al., 2014.

claim: Humans with germline mutations in STAT5B exhibit a range of clinical abnormalities.
source: Consistent with the latter point, humans with germline mutations in STAT5B exhibit a range of clinical abnormalities, indicating that STAT5A cannot compensate for some vital functions (Kanai et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kanai et al., 2012.

claim: STAT5A cannot compensate for some vital functions of STAT5B in humans.
source: Consistent with the latter point, humans with germline mutations in STAT5B exhibit a range of clinical abnormalities, indicating that STAT5A cannot compensate for some vital functions (Kanai et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that humans with STAT5B mutations have clinical abnormalities, supported by citation to Kanai et al., 2012.

claim: Compound STAT5 deficiency manifests striking immunological abnormalities in mice, most notably lymphopenia, splenomegaly and autoimmunity.
source: Compound STAT5 deficiency manifests striking immunological abnormalities in mice, most notably lymphopenia, splenomegaly and autoimmunity. These are typically attributed to its role downstream of the common gamma chain (ɣc) receptor and its dedicated Janus kinase, Jak3 (Moriggl et al., 1999b; Snow et al., 2003; Yao et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Moriggl et al., 1999b; Snow et al., 2003; Yao et al., 2006.

claim: The immunological abnormalities in compound STAT5 deficiency are typically attributed to its role downstream of the common gamma chain (ɣc) receptor and Jak3.

claim: The ɣc is shared by 6 different cytokines: IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15 and IL-21.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rochman et al., 2009.

claim: Each ɣc cytokine employs a unique co-receptor subunit that determines which cell types can respond.

claim: The ɣc-STAT5 axis promotes Th1- and Th2-type effector responses in CD4+ helper T cells.

evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations including Moriggl et al., 1999a; Liao et al., 2008; 2011.

evidence: The claim is based on experimental observation (data not shown) and supported by citations to Hoelbl et al., 2006; Cui et al., 2004.

claim: All 8 genotypes of STAT5 mutant mice survived beyond 6 months of age.

evidence: The claim is based on experimental observation (data not shown) and supported by citations to Hoelbl et al., 2006; Cui et al., 2004.

evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Stat5b is required for immunological tolerance in mice.
source: Therefore, as in humans, Stat5b is required for immunological tolerance in mice but, given the clear difference between having one or two Stat5a alleles, redundancy and/or cooperativity is also evident.

claim: Redundancy and/or cooperativity between Stat5a and Stat5b is evident in immunological tolerance.

claim: One-allele Stat5b-deficient mice had fewer splenocytes than WT controls.

claim: Two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice had fewer splenocytes than WT controls.

claim: Cell counts were reduced in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.

claim: STAT5A has substantial influence on splenocyte cellularity.
source: Cell counts were also reduced in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice, suggesting that, while STAT5B may be dominant, STAT5A does have substantial influence.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the reduced cell counts in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.

claim: All genotypes with less than three STAT5 alleles had reduced lymph node cell counts.

claim: Frequencies of CD4+ T cells were comparable across all STAT5 mutant genotypes.

claim: CD8+ T cells were reduced in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: CD8+ T cells were reduced to a lesser extent in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice compared to one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: B cells were increased in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: GL7+ Fashigh IgDlow germinal center (GC) B cells were dramatically enriched in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: One-allele Stat5a-deficient mice had a more modest accumulation of GC B cells compared to one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: There was a marked accumulation of CD44high IL-7Rαlow effector/memory T cells in Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: The accumulation of effector/memory T cells was more pronounced in Stat5b-deficient mice bearing one-allele of Stat5a than in those bearing two.

claim: IFN-ɣ+ cells were highly enriched in the autoimmune-prone Stat5b-deficient mice but not age-matched Stat5a-deficient counterparts.
source: IFN-ɣ+ cells were highly enriched in the autoimmune-prone Stat5b-deficient mice but not age-matched Stat5a-deficient counterparts, suggesting that STAT5B may be particularly important for limiting Th1-type responses.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: STAT5B may be particularly important for limiting Th1-type responses.

claim: IL-17A+ Th17-type cells were increased in Stat5b-deficient mice but this trend did not reach statistical significance.

claim: There was dramatic accumulation of PD1high CXCR5high ICOShigh Tfh cells in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: There was a more modest enrichment of Tfh cells in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice compared to one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: Mice lacking one-allele each of Stat5a and Stat5b (double-heterozygotes) had more Tfh cells than those lacking two-alleles of Stat5a.

claim: The percentage of Tfh cells was comparable between two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.

claim: Two alleles of Stat5a are roughly equal to one allele of Stat5b in terms of Tfh cell regulation.

evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparable Tfh cell percentages between the two genotypes.

claim: STAT5 is essential for Treg cells.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Malek and Castro, 2010 and Mahmud et al., 2013.

claim: STAT5-null mice exhibit a profound lack of Treg cells.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yao et al., 2007; Burchill et al., 2006.

claim: Frequencies of splenic FOXP3+ cells were relatively normal across STAT5 mutants.

claim: Absolute counts of Treg cells were significantly lower in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.

claim: IL-2Rα is a component of the IL-2 receptor that is critical for Treg cell homeostasis and function.

It is also a both upstream and downstream of STAT5 signaling and, thus, can be viewed as an indicator of STAT5 activity (Malek and Castro, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Malek and Castro, 2010.

claim: IL-2Rα is both upstream and downstream of STAT5 signaling.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Malek and Castro, 2010.

evidence: The claim is inferred from the relationship between IL-2Rα and STAT5 signaling, supported by citation to Malek and Castro, 2010.

claim: The percentage of IL-2Rα+ Treg cells mirrored the total number of Stat5 alleles.
